correctness.rationale: For a uniform k-block partition of [n], an edge equality event has probability p=S(n-1,k)/S(n,k), and two distinct edges (incident or disjoint) have joint probability q=S(n-2,k)/S(n,k), by contractions of rank two. The n-1 edges in each spanning tree create (n-1)^2 ordered pairs, t identical, yielding Cov=t(p-q)-(n-1)^2(p^2-q). Strict Stirling log-concavity at fixed k gives c=p^2-q>0. The global monochromatic-pair count R over N=n(n-1)/2 edges satisfies Var(R)=Np(1-p)-N(N-1)c>=0 and hence tau=(n-1)^2 c/(p-q) <=2(n-1)/n<2; signs are negative for t=0, positive for t>=2, and variable for t=1. Equality at k=n-1 follows R=1; k=2 n>=6 gives tau<1. Separately enumerated all partitions and exact rational covariances for n=3..7 for a path/star tree pair. Feasible t depends on n and trees; no claim for excluded k=1,n or full bivariate law.
